data.name: Wonfourn
data.detailed_description:
Está na hora de cumprir seu destino e embarcar em uma grande aventura atrás de fama, fortuna e glória. O primogênito de cada uma das grandes nações de Wonfourn alcançou a maioridade. Escolha bem, porque cada um tem diferentes pontos fortes. Chegou o momento de testar sua força e provar seu valor em uma busca épica pela sobrevivência. Navegue e explore 36 ilhas, cada uma com seus próprios desafios e surpresas. Proteja seu reino com a vida! Domine o arco e flecha e a lança em uma RV gloriosa. Negocie mercadorias com outras ilhas, descubra e explore rotas comerciais e fique atento aos bandos de piratas atrás dos seus tesouros. Controle batalhas do convés do seu navio e sinta o rugir dos canhões para fazer pedacinho dos seus adversários. Cruze o oceano à procura de riquezas e gaste sua fortuna nos melhores armamentos para sentir o gostinho da vitória nas batalhas. A derrota não é uma opção!

CARACTERÍSTICAS PRINCIPAIS

  • 36 ilhas para explorar
  • 6 nações para jogar
  • Expedições empolgantes
  • Comércio com mercadores
  • Piratas e batalhas marítimas
  • Justas, lançamento de lança e tiro com arco
  • Forja do ferreiro

reviews.review:
[h1] Experienced on the Oculus Rift with Touch Controllers [/h1]

Have you ever wondered what would happen if Skyrim and Black Flag were mixed together with mostly dreams and a low shoe-string budget and released to VR? Well, no need to wonder any longer. This is the game that answers that question. So is the game so bad that it's bad or is it so bad that it's good?

It's closer to good than bad actually. This game is ambitious if nothing else. There's totally epic moments (as long as you use your imagination) like when a dragon appears from the sky as you're sailing the open seas. You land on an island where a wench asks you to come inside her establishment. You get ideas in your head. Where is this going? Am I going up to her room? 

No, you get a quest to try some jousting. So you get a view of being on a horse and a knight's armored helmet on your head as your horse automatically gallops you towards your opponent. You reach out and aim for his head via mostly gaze aim although somehow the touch controllers play a role. I was confused by the whole thing. Needless to say, I easily won gold off that deal.

Then you visit a Wolf king who asks you to free the slaves. So you sail north and go to another island that looks almost exactly the same as the first one. Except this one has chickens/roosters instead of sheep roaming around. You notice the day and night cycle that looks like the world is spinning around in minutes. It rains a lot in this world. You go again to the wench who must have twin sisters all around. You get another quest except this time you're throwing spears at Orcs. You finally get enough gold by bartering goods with the local merchant.

Then you're off to buy and free slaves, when you run into pirates out in the open sea. Good thing you bought some cannonballs .... so you can shoot and blow through your gold as the pirates take more of yours. Good thing that you can also pound swords and make some gold slowly but surely. 

Are there more quests / adventures to be had? I don't know but a lot of stuff already repeated itself. I'm sure the quest to free slaves goes somewhere if you can avoid losing all your gold to the pirates. This game had some genuinely fun moments for me, mixed with moments of sheer frustration and despair.

I only paid $4 so I think i got my money's worth (bargain deal if you have bought this dev's other games). Yeah, I have bought all his other games. This one is actually his best one. The rest are pretty bad (except renzo racer if you can find it under .50 cents)

Rate 6/10. It could potentially be really good, like seriously epic. But hey, even now, it's so bad that it's good. Especially if you can get it at $4 (4.16 to be precise) like I did. I would give it a 5/10 at the current normal sale price of $10.
